name: Yugoslav Partisans
native: Narodnooslobodilačka vojska i partizanski odredi Jugoslavije

successors.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)
successors.text: the new Yugoslavia: 'By the end of the war, the Partisans had gained control of the entire country as well as Trieste and Carinthia' (page A)

ledger.x: 22 June 1941: the first Partisan uprising, in the Brezovica woods between Sisak and Zagreb.
17 November 1941: the Main National Liberation Committee for Serbia is founded in Užice, seat of the short-lived republic of the liberated west.
By 29 November 1941: German forces suppress the uprising and the republic of Užice, the first liberated territory in Europe, falls.
1942: after the Second Enemy Offensive (January to early February) the Partisan headquarters moves to Foča.
4 November 1942: the Partisans win at Bihać and found the so-called Bihać Republic in the heart of the NDH.
January to April 1943: the Fourth Enemy Offensive drives the Partisans out of western Bosnia and the Bihać Republic.
By September 1943: Tito's headquarters are near Drvar in western Bosnia.
October to December 1944: the Partisans, with British artillery, stem the Germans and liberate Risan and Podgorica, taking Montenegro.
1944: the Partisan-held interior of the NDH, the land its 1944 shape no longer holds.
20 October 1944: the Red Army and the Partisans liberate Belgrade in the Belgrade Offensive.
Winter 1944: Vardar Macedonia, North Macedonia today, passes to the Partisans.
Winter 1944: the Partisans hold most of the Dalmatian coast.
Winter 1944: the front in Syrmia freezes between the Partisans and the Wehrmacht and NDH forces.
8 March 1945: the coalition government meets in Belgrade.
March 1945: the Partisans merge into the Yugoslav state: the National Liberation Army becomes the Yugoslav Army on 1 March and a coalition government forms in Belgrade on 8 March.

wars.name: Partisan uprising of 1941 in western Serbia (Republic of Užice)
wars.outcome: German forces suppressed the uprising by 29 November 1941 and the short-lived republic of the liberated west fell.

wars.name: Fourth Enemy Offensive (Battle of the Neretva)
wars.outcome: The offensive pushed the Partisans from western Bosnia toward the Neretva; 'This took place from January to April, 1943.'

wars.name: Seventh Enemy Offensive (Operation Rösselsprung)
wars.outcome: An unsuccessful attempt to eliminate Tito personally, in western Bosnia in the second quarter of 1944 (late May); no border moved.

wars.name: Belgrade Offensive
wars.outcome: The Red Army and the Partisans liberated Belgrade on 20 October 1944 and the Partisans then controlled Serbia.

wars.name: Syrmian Front
wars.outcome: The Wehrmacht and NDH forces fortified a front in Syrmia that held through the winter of 1944-45.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line bounds the Partisans: liberated areas, guerrilla zones and fronts are approximate.
